subject: Close-path stability check-in — MAP rebaseline request & escalation
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@cloudworks.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP milestone at risk — procurement delay

Irene / team,

Quick heads-up from procurement: our legal + procurement teams just flagged a line-item in the SOW that will add a 1–2 week review before signatures. That pushes the previously agreed-on procurement milestone and puts the target close date (Apr 6) at risk.

We still want to close but need to understand options: can we (a) get a short-term interim agreement (MOU) to unblock PO work, or (b) accept a one-week extension to the close with priority onboarding?

Attaching their high-level procurement notes for context (procurement_notes.pdf). Happy to jump on a quick call today.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of IT — CloudWorks
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@cloudworks.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone at risk — procurement delay

Tom — thanks for flagging and for the notes. We should be able to avoid a hard stall, but we need to align the MAP and formalize fallbacks. Proposed immediate actions:

- Short call (30m) today to agree whether an MOU will unblock the team or if a one-week close extension is acceptable.
- I will prepare a MAP rebaseline (map_v2.xlsx) showing two paths: expedited PO path and extension path with corresponding deliverables and success criteria.
- If procurement insists on language changes, we can propose a conditional 7-day extension and offer prioritized onboarding and one week of waived support fees as a limited concession.

Please confirm availability for a 11:30am or 3pm PT call. I’ll share the rebaseline spreadsheet and a brief risk register (close_risk_log.csv) ahead of the call.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@cloudworks.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone at risk — procurement delay

Irene — available at 3pm PT and agree with the two-path approach. From a mitigation perspective:

- Operational fallback: we can schedule onboarding work to start against a deposit invoice to keep the engineering window without a signed PO. Finance would need sign-off but we've done similar for three enterprise deals in the last quarter.
- Commercial fallback: we can offer a single week of waived production support fees (noting that long-term credits require manager approval).
- Escalation: recommend we pull Laura Bennett into the thread if the external procurement team is unwilling to consider conditional language. Laura can approve limited commercial concessions.

I’ll prepare an annotated timeline in the rebaseline showing resource ramp and the critical-path tasks.

—Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@cloudworks.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone at risk — procurement delay

Thanks team — short summary and ask from CS side:

- If CloudWorks agrees to an MOU allowing a deposit/conditional start, we can onboard the pilot team week of Mar 29 and preserve the original onboarding windows.
- If procurement requires a full PO before any work, a one-week slip to Apr 13 is manageable if we (a) get written confirmation of the new timeline and (b) get a prioritized onboarding slot flagged in the MAP (we’ll move the onboarding tasks to "priority: high").

I’ve attached the rebaseline spreadsheet (map_v2.xlsx) with both options and a CSV risk log showing probability/impact for each risk (close_risk_log.csv).

Quoted for context below.

--

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@cloudworks.io>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: approval request — one-week extension + prioritized onboarding (CloudWorks, D-8492)

Laura — looping you in for quick approval. Procurement at CloudWorks is requiring an additional clause that would add a 7–14 day legal review. The customer prefers either an MOU to unblock or a one-week close extension.

My ask: approve a one-week extension to the target close date (new target Apr 13) and authorize up to $20,000 in one-time onboarding/priority credits if we need to concede commercially. This will keep the MAP stable and protect our onboarding ROE.

Why this is important: if we don’t provide either path, we risk losing the original onboarding window (critical engineering capacity) which would push the entire delivery schedule by 3–4 weeks — much higher cost and churn risk. The attached close_risk_log.csv quantifies downstream impact.

Quick summary of options I recommended to the customer:
- Option A (preferred): sign MOU to allow deposit/onboarding to proceed; close on PO after legal review.
- Option B: accept 7-day extension to Apr 13; Redwood provides prioritized onboarding and up to $20k credit as one-time concession.

Please reply with APPROVE / DENY or QUESTIONS. If approved, I’ll update the MAP and HubSpot (link below) and send DocuSign for the MOU or revised SOW.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/D-8492
DocuSign (MOU draft): https://www.docusign.com/link/ABC-123-CloudWorks-MAP

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
